note: svg path data treats a relative l as absolute, so lines land at the raw numbers
anchor: let base = relative ? current : Point(x: 0, y: 0)

note: svg path data S skips reflecting the previous control point and uses the current point
svg path data arc sweep flag inverted, so the centre goes on the wrong side of the chord
svg path data arc ignores the large-arc flag and always takes the short way
anchor: let largeArc = try flag(), sweep = try flag()
replacement: let largeArc = try flag() && false, sweep = try flag()

note: svg path data arc skips scaling up radii too small for the chord
svg path data arc drops the finite-centre guard, so extreme chords fail later with a vague message
anchor: guard [delta, centre.x, centre.y, rx, ry].allSatisfy(\.isFinite) else { throw damaged("arc centre out of range") }

note: svg path data arc swaps rx and ry in the centre formula, so ellipse arcs leave the ellipse
anchor: let centre = Point(x: coef * rx * p.y / ry, y: -coef * ry * p.x / rx)
replacement: let centre = Point(x: coef * ry * p.y / rx, y: -coef * rx * p.x / ry)
